You are auditing six proposed code fixes against the conventions and precedents established by a specific developer's work on this branch. You have NO prior context — build your own view from the code.

REPO: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`, branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`, HEAD `ac224a6`.

CONTEXT: Tim Lavelle is the project lead and a `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` member. He authored 14 commits in range `ec9d161..7b9b5dc` (103 files) that established most of the current footer/ui-kits/Contentful architecture. His commit messages are unusually detailed and frequently explain *why* a tradeoff was chosen. Three later commits (`49a95b9`, `5883499`, `ac224a6`) are by someone else.

A CodeRabbit review produced 14 findings. Six were verdicted **FIX**. Your job is to check each proposed fix against what Tim's code and commits actually establish, and flag any that would contradict a deliberate decision of his.

**THE CRITICAL DISTINCTION — apply it to every item:**
- **Convention / architecture / priority questions**: if Tim's code or commit messages establish a pattern, that pattern is authoritative. A proposed fix that breaks it should be re-verdicted to DECLINE or DEFER.
- **Empirical / factual questions**: a measurement stands regardless of who wrote the code. But you must still check whether Tim's commits show he *knowingly accepted* the behaviour as a tradeoff — quote it if so. "He considered and accepted this" changes the recommendation from "fix" to "raise with him", not to "ignore".

Be rigorous about the difference. Do not soften a factual finding because of authorship, and do not defend a stylistic preference against his established pattern.

THE SIX FIX VERDICTS TO AUDIT:

1. **#14 — `scripts/contentful/setup/bootstrapSpace.mjs`**: add `en-CA` to the provisioned locales. Claim: `seedRegions.mjs:42` writes `locale: 'en-CA'` for `ZimmermannUSIntl`, `bootstrapSpace.mjs` provisions 9 locales without it, and `pages/experience/index.tsx:94`→`:32` passes the site locale to the CDA, so `/en-ca/` Experience pages get an HTTP 400. Check: does Tim's own work show he knew? Search his commits and comments for `en-CA`, locale handling, and whether `bootstrapSpace.mjs` is even his file or pre-existing. Also check whether he deliberately left locale unpassed elsewhere (`hooks/useContentful.ts`, `components/footer/index.tsx`) as a staged decision.

2. **#13 — `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs:127-130`**: the validation gate `if (validation.items?.length && !FORCE && !(conflictingIds.length && TAKEOVER_IDS.length))` lets any non-conflict finding through whenever a `--takeover` is passed. Proposed: compute the unresolved set properly. Check whether Tim's commit message or code comments show this looseness was intentional (e.g. an escape hatch he wanted), and whether `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` — which he edited — describes the gate accurately.

3. **#10 — `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts:70-78`**: the tie-break warn and reassign both sit inside `if (candidateUpdatedAt > bestUpdatedAt)`, so equal timestamps silently keep whichever entry Contentful returned first, and the documented `console.warn` never fires in half the orderings. Proposed: hoist the warn, add `sys.id` as a stable secondary key. **This is Tim's file.** Read his JSDoc at `:46-50` and his tests in `resolveByRegion.test.ts` carefully — especially the test at `:84` named "order of the tied candidates in the input does not change the outcome". Did he intend order-dependence as acceptable? Does his own doc comment contradict his implementation? Quote both.

4. **#7 — `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:19`**: replace the literal `'uiCopy'` with the existing `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS.uiCopy` from `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts:53`. Check: who authored `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS`, does it have any consumers, and does Tim's code elsewhere use literals for content type IDs deliberately (check `pages/home/index.tsx`, `pages/experience/index.tsx`, `components/footer/index.tsx:183`)? If Tim consistently uses literals, this "fix" imposes a convention he didn't adopt.

5. **#8 — `overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.test.tsx`**: add `afterEach(() => vi.clearAllMocks())`. It's a provable no-op (the only mock is function-local). The argument for complying is a precedent set in commit `a207b9a` on `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts`. Check: is `a207b9a` Tim's commit or the other author's? Look at Tim's own test files — do they carry lifecycle hooks or not? If Tim's convention is "no hooks when there's nothing to reset", then complying contradicts the project lead's actual practice.

6. **#12 — `bootstrapSpace.mjs`**: reorder so locales are provisioned before environments are cloned, and loop over target environments. Check whether the current ordering is Tim's deliberate choice and whether any comment explains it.

CONSTRAINTS:
- **READ-ONLY.** No edits, staging, commits, stashes, checkouts. Other sessions are writing to this tree.
- **Do NOT run any script in `scripts/contentful/`** — they hit a live Contentful space. Read source only. Do not read `.env`, `.env.shared`, or `.env.<tier>`.
- You MAY run `npx vitest run`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, and `git log`/`git show`/`git blame`.

Use `git log --format='%h %an %s' ec9d161..7b9b5dc` and `git blame` to establish authorship of every file and line you reason about. Do not assume Tim wrote something because it's on this branch.

REPORT per finding: **UPHELD** (fix still right), **OVERTURNED** (Tim's precedent makes it wrong — say which precedent, quoted), or **RAISE WITH TIM** (factually real but he appears to have knowingly accepted it — quote the evidence). Include authorship for each file. Be terse and quote sources.

Audit complete. Nothing in the repo was touched — the empirical probe was transpiled to `/tmp/rbr_audit/` only.

## Authorship baseline

All 14 commits in `ec9d161..7b9b5dc` are `TimLavelle`. Every file in the six findings is Tim's, **except** the code that actually produces #14's failure. The precedent cited for #8 (`a207b9a`) is **Marcel's**, not Tim's.

---

### #14 — `bootstrapSpace.mjs` missing `en-CA` → **UPHELD**

Authorship: `bootstrapSpace.mjs` created by Tim `f81f6bc` (2026-07-12), touched `5640c25`. But the 400 chain is **not his**: `git blame` shows `experience/index.tsx:32` (`localeCode: locale`) and `:94-95` (`siteLocale?.id`) are **Marcel, `7ed19fa3`** (2026-07-31), and the `en-CA` locale itself arrived in **Marcel's `e4c342e`** (2026-08-07).

The gap is drift, not a decision. `contentfulMapping.generated.ts:8-19` has **10** `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` including `'en-CA'`; `bootstrapSpace.mjs:40-50` has exactly those 10 **minus** `en-CA`. Tim's list was complete when written — `en-CA` did not exist until 26 days later, and `e4c342e` updated `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` without updating `bootstrapSpace.mjs`. `config/sites.generated.js:52` confirms `en-CA` is a supported locale id for `ZimmermannUSIntl`, so `useMultiSite().locale.id` reaches the CDA as an unprovisioned locale.

No evidence Tim knowingly accepted it. His nearest touch (`5640c25`) was the adjacent `optional: !locale.default` payload flag, not the `LOCALES` array. He *did* show awareness of exactly this drift class in `seedRegions.mjs:35-38` — "copied 2026-08-23. Re-check that file if this list needs to change — it's autogenerated ... and this static copy can drift from it" — but that comment guards the region-entry list (which is correct, 11 entries incl. `en-CA`), not the space locales.

Two additions to the fix:
- **The fix is a no-op on 5 of 6 environments without #12.** `locale.create` is hardcoded to `'master'` (`:134`) and env creation is skipped on re-run, so adding `en-CA` reaches master only. `/en-ca/` keeps 400ing on dev/test/sit/staging/uat.
- `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md:111` is also stale and needs the same fix: *"Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE"* — says eleven, lists ten, omits `en-CA`.

---

### #13 — `installTemplate.mjs:127` validation gate → **UPHELD (claim overstated)**

Authorship: Tim, `5b2be3f`. Tier 2 — `protectedFiles.md` lists this exact path under *Contentful Schema Definitions (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — notify before changing)*.

I ran the real expression as a truth table. The claim "lets any non-conflict finding through whenever a `--takeover` is passed" is **too broad** — with only non-conflict findings present, `conflictingIds.length` is 0 and the gate still refuses. The genuine holes need ≥1 conflict finding co-present:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| 1 conflict + 1 **unrelated** finding, `--takeover` | **PROCEED** ← unrelated finding swallowed |
| 3 conflicts, `--takeover` covers only 1 | **PROCEED** ← 2 unadopted conflicts pass |
| non-conflict findings only, `--takeover` | REFUSE |

Not an intentional hatch. The intended hatch is named in the adjacent error at `:128` — *"Pass --force to override"* — so `--takeover` doubling as one is redundant, and its header docs (`:16-20`) scope it purely to adoption: *"Adopt it into the template explicitly rather than deleting it first."* No comment at `:127`. `protectedFiles.md` **does not describe the gate at all** (no mention of `--force`, `--takeover`, or validation), so there is no doc contradiction either way — but also nothing supporting the looseness.

Severity is moderate: Tim's own header states the conflict class is *"refused **by Contentful**"* server-side, so the local gate is pre-flight only. Reasonable to DEFER, not to decline.

---

### #10 — `resolveByRegion.ts:70-78` tie-break → **UPHELD (strongly)**

Authorship: Tim, `5b2be3f` / `5640c25`. His own doc and his own test name both assert invariants the implementation does not hold.

JSDoc `:47-50`:
> "Resolved **deterministically** by most-recently-updated rather than silently normalized — **a console.warn surfaces it** so the duplicate entry can be cleaned up."

Test `:84` name:
> "order of the tied candidates in the input does not change the outcome"

I transpiled the real module with esbuild and probed it:

```
A1 [older, newer] (his test :77)   winner=newer   warns=1
A2 [newer, older] (his test :84)   winner=newer   warns=0   ← warn never fires
B1 equal updatedAt [alpha, beta]   winner=alpha   warns=0
B2 equal updatedAt [beta, alpha]   winner=beta    warns=0   ← outcome flips, silently
C1/C2 no updatedAt                 flips with order, warns=0
```

He did **not** intend order-dependence. His test at `:84` declares order-independence as a desired property but only exercises **distinct** timestamps, so it passes while B1/B2 is a live counterexample to the property its own name asserts. Both suites are green today (13 tests pass) — the hole is invisible to the existing suite, which is precisely the "survives a refactor invisibly if broken" case `testing.md` says to test.

Aggravating: `footer/index.tsx:183` calls `getEntries({content_type: 'footerConfig', include: 3})` with **no `order` param**, so CDA return order isn't contractually stable — the warn's firing is nondeterministic across requests in production. Both halves of the proposed fix (hoist the warn; add `sys.id` as secondary key) are justified by his own stated intent.

---

### #7 — `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:19` literal vs `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` → **OVERTURNED**

Authorship: `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` scaffold is Tim `f81f6bc`; **Tim populated all five members himself in `5b2be3f`** (blame `:54-58`).

It has **zero consumers** repo-wide — only its own definition and the derived `ContentTypeId` type, itself also unused. Tim then used bare literals at every call site he wrote *after* populating it:
- `footer/index.tsx:183` — `content_type: 'footerConfig'` (`5640c25`, one commit later)
- `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:19` — `useContentfulEntries<UiCopyEntry>('uiCopy')` (`90069b2`, three commits later)

Pre-existing sites match: `pages/home/index.tsx:148` uses `'homepage'` and `experience/index.tsx:17` uses a module-local `EXPERIENCE_TYPE_ID = 'collectionPageExp'` — **neither is in the registry**, so it isn't maintained as a source of truth either.

The fix imposes a convention its own author declined at 2/2 of his call sites, and would leave 3 of 4 sites inconsistent — partial adoption is worse than either end state. Each literal appears exactly once, so there's no DRY payoff. Re-verdict **DECLINE**; the real question (adopt the registry at all 4 sites and add the 2 missing IDs, or delete it as dead code) is a separate decision for Tim.

---

### #8 — `useUiCopy.test.tsx` add `afterEach(vi.clearAllMocks)` → **OVERTURNED**

The cited precedent is **not Tim's**. `a207b9a` is Marcel's, and its own message concedes the change is decorative:
> "This file's resolvers are pure and it mocks nothing, so **the hooks reset no observable state** — added for consistency with the rule as written rather than for isolation."

Tim's practice, in the 6 test files he wrote the day *after* that precedent landed, is the opposite. Hooks appear only where they reset real state:
- `useZimmModal.test.tsx` — captures/restores `document.body.style.overflow` (load-bearing)
- `resolveByRegion.test.ts` — `spyOn(console.warn)` + `restoreAllMocks`, scoped to the inner `describe` only
- `footer/`, `zimmSubscribeSection/`, `uiCopyProvider/` — 14-15 `vi.*` calls each

And no hooks where there's nothing to reset: `useSubscribeSection.test.ts`, `recipeGuards.test.ts`, `useUiCopy.test.tsx`. The decisive counterexample is **`footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx`** — Tim's, carries a real module-level `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', …)`, and **still has no `beforeEach`/`afterEach`/`clearAllMocks`**.

Re-verdict **DECLINE**. Caveat worth surfacing: `testing.md:67` does still state it unqualified — *"Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test."* Tim edited `testing.md` in `542ac65` (+28 lines) and left that line alone. So the durable fix is qualifying the rule text, which is Tier 1 governance and needs Tim — not adding a no-op to satisfy a rule its own author ignores in practice.

---

### #12 — `bootstrapSpace.mjs` provision locales before cloning → **UPHELD**

Authorship: Tim, `f81f6bc`. Not in `protectedFiles.md` (unlike `installTemplate.mjs`), so no Tier 2 gate.

The only comment touching the ordering asserts the opposite of what the order delivers — `:104`:
```
// ── 2. Locales (set up in master; cloned environments inherit them) ─────────
```
Step 1 clones all 5 environments from master (`:96`) *before* step 2 creates locales in master (`:134`). Clones inherit locales as of clone time, so the stated inheritance can't happen on a first run. Worse, the file claims *"Idempotent — safe to re-run"* (`:6`) but cannot converge: env creation is skipped on re-run and `locale.create` is hardcoded to `'master'`, so a locale added later **never** reaches the 5 existing environments.

Nothing suggests deliberateness. Two signals point the other way: `_shared.mjs:85` already defines `getExistingLocaleCodes(client, environmentId)` **parameterised by environment** while the call site at `:107` hardcodes `'master'`; and Tim's later-generation script `seedRegions.mjs:5-8` is explicitly per-environment — *"entries are a separate concern and have to be seeded per environment after that environment's `region` content type exists."*

Empirical caveat: the real dev space evidently *does* have `en` (Tim's `5b2be3f` reports *"region entries seeded"*, which writes `{en: …}` fields into `--target dev`), so master must have had `en` before the clones were made. That means the bug hasn't bitten yet — it bites on the *next* locale added, which is exactly `en-CA`.

---

## Bottom line

| # | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| #14 | **UPHELD** | Not Tim's gap — traces to `e4c342e`/`7ed19fa3` (Marcel). Ineffective without #12. Also fix `02-contentful.md:111`. |
| #13 | **UPHELD** | Claim overstated: needs ≥1 conflict co-present. `--force` is the intended hatch. Tier 2 — notify Integration/SI. |
| #10 | **UPHELD** | Contradicts Tim's own JSDoc *and* his own test name; proven empirically. Highest-confidence fix of the six. |
| #7 | **OVERTURNED → DECLINE** | Tim populated the registry then used literals at 2/2 of his own call sites; registry has 0 consumers and omits 2 in-use IDs. |
| #8 | **OVERTURNED → DECLINE** | Precedent is Marcel's and self-described as resetting nothing; Tim omits hooks even with a real `vi.mock`. Fix the rule text instead. |
| #12 | **UPHELD** | Sole relevant comment asserts inheritance the ordering defeats; helper already parameterised. |

Four uphelds, two overturns — and the two overturns are exactly the two stylistic items, while all four uphelds are behavioural. Sequencing note: **#12 must land with or before #14**, or #14 fixes nothing outside master.
